newsitem.title: USA: Entergy files for competition in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Entergy files for competition in Texas.

text.p: Entergy Corp said on Friday that it filed a plan with the Public Utility Commission of Texas to open competition for electrical power there.

In its filing, Entergy commits to establishing retail competition, service quality standards, a regional power exchange and an independent system operator covering, at a minimum, areas included in the Southwest Power Pool, Entergy said.
Entergy said it has asked the commission for a reciprocal commitment ensuring the company can fully recover its prudently incurred investments approved by regulators.
The plan will require approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Entergy said.

If the plan is approved by the Public Utility Commission of Texas and other agencies do not act by the end of seven years, Entergy said it will still provide electricity in Texas based on market prices or cost-based prices, whichever is lower, Entergy said.

Entergy had filed a "Transition to Competition" plan in November that called for a cap on base rates for seven years, a performance plan for its River Bend power plant, a mechanism to prevent cost shifting from large customers to residential customers and businesses, and accelerated recovery of River Bend power plant costs.
